gloss: end of the Edo period, late Tokugawa era

definitions.gloss: end of the Edo period, late Tokugawa era
definitions.explanation: The final years of the Tokugawa shogunate, roughly from the 1850s to 1868. A turbulent period marked by the arrival of Western powers, internal political upheaval, and the eventual fall of the shogunate leading to the Meiji Restoration.

examples.japanese: {幕末|ばくまつ}の{志士|しし}たちを{描|えが}いた{小説|しょうせつ}。
examples.english: A novel depicting the patriots of the late Edo period.

examples.japanese: {幕末|ばくまつ}から{明治|めいじ}にかけて、{日本|にほん}は{急速|きゅうそく}に{近代化|きんだいか}した。
examples.english: From the end of the Edo period through the Meiji era, Japan rapidly modernized.

examples.japanese: {幕末|ばくまつ}には{尊王攘夷|そんのうじょうい}を{掲|かか}げる{勢力|せいりょく}と{開国|かいこく}{派|は}が{激|はげ}しく{対立|たいりつ}した。
examples.english: At the end of the Edo period, forces advocating reverence for the emperor and expulsion of foreigners fiercely clashed with the pro-opening faction.

notes:
CULTURE:
The {幕末|ばくまつ} era (roughly 1853–1868) began with the arrival of Commodore Perry's "Black Ships" and ended with the {明治維新|めいじいしん} (Meiji Restoration). Key figures of this period — such as {坂本龍馬|さかもとりょうま}, {西郷隆盛|さいごうたかもり}, and {新選組|しんせんぐみ} — remain enormously popular in Japanese historical fiction, TV dramas, manga, and films.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幕末|ばくまつ}の{志士|しし}: patriots of the late Edo period
- {幕末|ばくまつ}{維新|いしん}: late Edo period and Restoration
- {幕末|ばくまつ}{期|き}: the Bakumatsu period
